note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: Treasury official: Sept deficit -$26.9B beat (-$34.7B fcst); FY26 $1.992T largest in 5 years (~6.2% GDP); tariff refunds $145B; debt service record $1.36T. France OAT-Bund 135.2bp; Oct 20 revenue vote, Moody's Oct 23.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US IP +0.7% beat (6th straight gain) vs NY Fed services -20.7 warning — factories up, services flashing. UK GDP +0.1% beat (2.1% y/y, strongest since Aug 2022); NZ PMI 56.5 (strongest since 2021). China Q3 GDP next week.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: Hot week: US CPI 3.7%, PPI +1.3% (6.3% y/y), import prices +1.1% (+8.1% y/y, 4-yr high). Eurozone CPI 3.8% confirmed (energy +18.9%). WTI back over $100 — the energy kicker into every Oct/Nov meeting.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%, Reuters Fri) into Saturday's blackout; December the debate. ECB: no October hike priced — December 100%, ≥1 more by April (Reuters bond report). BoC Oct 28 live (Macklem hawkish + WTI >$100); BoE Nov 5 on the GDP beat; RBNZ Oct 28 two-way; BoJ Oct 29-30 (Ueda overshoot risks). Goolsbee 6pm ET the last voice before blackout.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: DXY's first weekly fall in five. Contrarian flag: hedge funds net LONG AUD (79th pctile) — squeeze thesis broken, pain trade is down. Dollar 54th, euro 44th, yen 67th, franc 41st, CAD 31st — none crowded (CFTC TFF, Oct 6).
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Relief: Asia rebounded (Kospi +2.8%) from the AI rout; Iran-escalation fears eased → DXY first weekly fall in five. Underneath: Hormuz at 68% of baseline flows, Houthi Aden strike, oil >$100 — CHF +1.4% in two sessions.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Nov WTI +2.8% to $100.71 (first >$100 in a month) on Ukraine refinery strikes; Dec Brent +3.2% to $109.28. Brent-WTI ~$10.7 = wide geopolitical premium. Vitol: Hormuz fuel-oil flows down ≥800k t/month; IEA 100M-bbl release + shadow-fleet easing talk cap it.
tot.title: Terms of trade
